original.target_description: Single reported study: Presentation Duration × Facial Expression interaction in attentional bias scores among high-EM White participants, comparing neutral versus happy expressions across short and long presentation durations.

n.sample_role: Final high-EM White participants in the repeated-measures subgroup interaction. Low-EM participants are a separate group, excluded from this subgroup test.
n.exclusions: Thirty participants recruited; one high-EM and one low-EM participant removed for extremely slow latencies after more than 50% of their data had been removed or transformed. Incorrect responses and latencies above 1,500 ms deleted (1% of data); remaining extremes replaced at 750 or 100 ms (1.3% of data). Final groups: 14 high-EM and 14 low-EM.
n.location: Printed p. 100 (text page 3), Results final-sample paragraph; high-EM interaction continues on p. 101.

notes: Identity assessment: canonical text is the full five-page primary Research Report, The Threat of Appearing Prejudiced and Race-Based Attentional Biases, by Jennifer A. Richeson and Sophie Trawalter, Psychological Science, Volume 19 Number 2, pp. 98–102, copyright 2008. Title, authors, year, journal, and pagination match the neutral reference. DOI is not printed in the supplied text and cannot be independently confirmed under the cache-only restriction. SOURCE_URL names the Northwestern author-hosted PDF. No PDF path supplied for rendering. Target identified from high-EM subgroup and facial-expression comparison, not row order or numeric matching. Relevant interaction: F(1, 13) 5 8.16, prep 5 .97, d 5 1.58. The printed prep (p_rep) is distinct from conventional p; no conversion performed. No conventional same-test p is printed. Figure 1 caption p < .05 (one-tailed) concerns bias scores against zero, not this interaction. Neutral-only duration test F(1, 13) 5 7.64, prep 5 .95, d 5 1.53 is a different test. N = 14 is directly printed for the final high-EM subgroup; no df-derived N or group sum. Unassigned sides/fields are placeholders only.
